title: Rapid Pilot Toolkit — Deck Brainstorm
body:
Purpose: rapid one-page deck and pocket toolkit sellers can deploy in the first 48–72 hours of a pilot. Focus: reduce time-to-first-value, prove SLOs (latency/cost/quality), and create repeatable handoffs to Solutions/SEs.

Audience: AE + SE for mid-market and platform engineering buyers. Primary scenario: 6–12 week technical pilot (hosted -> dedicated decision) where buyer is evaluating latency/cost tradeoffs and safe fallbacks.

Structure (slide by slide / pocket card):
- Cover / TL;DR (30s): what we deliver in the pilot, success criteria, expected timeline (week 0,1,2,4,6).
- Quick win checklist (48–72h): test endpoints, sample prompts, perf smoke test, embed sampling (if applicable), basic observability hooks (token counts + latency tracing).
- SLOs & acceptance criteria (template): 95th latency target, cost per 1k tokens target, qualitative quality baseline (closed set of 20 eval prompts).
- Canary & fallback plan (engineer-friendly runbook): model variant routing, hot fallback sequence, telemetry checks that trigger fallback, rollback steps.
- Data security checklist: VPC toggle, TLS endpoints, sample IP allowlist flow, simple KMS validation steps.
- Cost levers cheat-sheet: batching suggestions, KV cache hints, quantization options and quality/cost impact estimates.
- Pilot success narrative (customer-facing): what to show executives on week 2, week 6 (latency graphs, cost delta, example responses).
- Handoff playbook to Dedicated/Private: artifacts to capture (prompts, traces, representative traffic), recommended reserved capacity sizing heuristic, rollout plan.
- Objection scripts: short scripts for 5 common objections (latency risk, cost uncertainty, vendor lock-in/regulatory).
- Field notes & rapid diagnostics: 10 one-liners for SEs to triage common pilot breakages.

Rapid win checklist (detailed):
1) Create pilot token and share minimal API snippet (node/python) — include timeout and streaming option.
2) Run 10 representative requests, capture sample responses + token counts.
3) Run perf smoke (single-client load test): 50 concurrent short sessions for 2 minutes; capture 50/95/99 latencies.
4) Attach one dashboard link and enable trace sampling at 1% by default.
5) Define 20 evaluation prompts (customer-sourced + our standard set) and run local eval to establish baseline.

SLO template (fill-in fields):
- 95th latency target: ____ ms
- Average cost / 1k tokens: $____
- Quality regressed vs baseline: <= ____% (per prompt-suite)
- Uptime: ____% (pilot length)

Canary & fallback (playbook sketch):
- Default route: high-quality model (hq-1) hosted.
- Canary route: lower-cost quantized variant (q-1) at 5% traffic.
- Telemetry triggers to shift: 95p latency > target for 10m OR error rate > 1% sustained 5m.
- Automated fallback: shift canary -> 100% hq-1 for 10m, send alert to SE and AE.
- Post-incident: attach sample requests that failed, run local reproducer, capture KV cache metrics.

Example objection scripts (short):
- "Latency is too unpredictable" -> "We baseline with your traffic pattern in the first 48–72 hours, and the pilot includes a performance smoke test plus a canary that automatically routes to a higher-SLA variant on triggers — you stay online while we tune."
- "We’re worried about cost surprises" -> "We set a hard cap on pilot spend and instrument per-route token tracking. The quick cost levers card shows two immediate knobs: batching window and a quantized model variant that’s 30–50% cheaper for similar prompt types."

Pilot timeline (recommended):
- Day 0: Kickoff, share sample code, set up dashboard + traces, agree on eval prompts.
- Day 1–3: Quick wins checklist completion + perf smoke test.
- Week 1: First quality report + canary traffic test.
- Week 2–3: Tuned routing, quantization experiments (non-blocking), capture exec summary.
- Week 4–6: Scale stress tests, cost modeling, finalize Dedicated sizing if moving forward.

Field diagnostics cheat-sheet (10 lines):
- "High 95p latency" -> check batching window and sequence length distribution.
- "High error spikes" -> inspect tokenization errors, pay attention to unusually long system prompts.
- "Cost blowout" -> evaluate token counts per request vs expected; enable quantized route.
- "Quality regression" -> rerun the 20 eval prompts, compare n-gram and semantic diff.
- "DNS/timeouts" -> validate VPC egress and firewall rules.

Deck voice & design notes (for the final slide pack):
- Keep slides concise: 1 idea per slide, 3–4 bullets. Use real screenshots from pilot dashboards (latency histograms, top tokens).
- Add a one-slide appendix with the exact API snippet and a link to the reproducible load script in GitHub.
- Tone: pragmatic, engineer-friendly, and measurable. Avoid abstract marketing claims.

Open questions / follow-ups (to resolve before first draft):
- Which sample eval prompts should be default for fintech vs. SaaS vs. search-heavy workloads? (assign Priya)
- Can we add a togglable budget-cap feature in the hosted panel for pilots? (ask infra/product — Miguel)
- Need a pre-approved legal blurb for pilot data handling for enterprise customers (Legal).

Action items & owners (short):
- Draft 1-page quick wins card (Aisha) due 2025-02-17.
- Populate 20-eval prompt library with category tags (Priya) due 2025-02-20.
- Hook up sample dashboard and add screenshots to the deck (Jordan) due 2025-02-24.
- Confirm legal blurb and link (AE template) (Miguel) due 2025-02-28.

Notes to self / rough lines for slide text:
- "Pilot promise: measurable perf & cost visibility in 72 hours — not a black box trial."
- "We prioritize predictable economics: set your SLO, we help you hit it."
- "Fallback-first: we assume failures and design a safe route to keep the app online."

Slack threads and refs: #sales-pilots, #infra-canary, Confluence pilot-templates, GH repo pilot-scripts.

Appendix (examples to paste into one-slide appendix):
- Minimal Node curl snippet (with timeout) — copy/paste.
- Quick curl to trigger canary header (x-routing: canary).
- Link to reproducible load script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pilot-scripts/tree/main/quick-smoke

End of brainstorm — this doc should evolve into two deliverables: a one-page pocket card (printable / PDF) and a 10-slide deck for AE+SE. Keep it tight, ship fast, iterate from pilot feedback.
